newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Oil steadies after slide but outlook bearish.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Oil steadies after slide but outlook bearish.

text.p: World oil prices steadied slightly on Friday after hitting nine-month lows earlier in the week but brokers said the outlook was still bearish for next week with crude supply outweighing demand.

London futures for benchmark Brent crude blend traded at $18.23 per barrel by 1704 GMT -- a rise of five cents over Thursday's settlement. May Brent lost 32 cents on Thursday, extending a slide of 59 cents a day earlier.
Brent has lost 25 percent of its value in the space of three months, having crumpled $6.50 in the three months to hit a nine-month low.

"After the sharp sell-off we saw earlier this week we see short-term consolidation in the market. However, the view is still bearish," said Nauman Barakat, vice president of energy futures trading at Prudential Securities in New York.
Brokers said heavier shipments of Iraqi crude oil under the United Nations oil-for-food deal, now in its fourth month, could push crude prices down further.
Iraq is expected to increase oil sales next month in order to meet the $2 billion target permitted by the U.N. under the exchange.
"With the possibility of more Iraqi oil sales the crude market could come under more downward pressure sometime next week," Barakat said.

Analysts say extra supplies are outrunning rising world demand as fresh crude outlets appear from all corners of the globe with the help of technology developments that allow new fields onstream faster and cheaper.

One factor that pressured oil prices during the week was news that Saudi Arabia -- the world's largest crude producer -- had cut its selling prices and European and U.S. traders were struggling to find crude buyers.
Saudi Arabian Light crude on Thursday for European buyers was valued at just over $15 a barrel compared to $23 in early January, a 35 percent slump.

In London, some brokers said the May Brent futures contract would test the psychologically-important $18 target sometime soon. The May contract dipped as low as $18.07 on Thursday, a level not seen since June 25 last year.
"It will test $18 at some point. It may not go through it but it will have a look at $18 either this week or the start of next week," one broker said.
"I don't know if it will fall below $18 next week but I am looking at a neutral market with a 40-cent range," another dealer said.
